Derrière Tech 45', il y a Sébastien Coua: Behind Tech 45' is Sébastien Couasnon — and that's no detail. A seasoned tech journalist formerly at BFM Business, he covered digital news for years and saw several cycles, several bubbles, several "definitive revolutions" come and go. Now independent with Orso Media, his podcast follows that logic: step back, take the long view, and let the people who make tech speak, not just those who comment on it.
Le concept a une particularité : le form: The concept has one particularity: the format (almost) never changes — and that's its strength. Every week, an executive or C-level from a French tech company, 45 minutes on the clock, always the same structure: the career path, the company's story, what works, what's stuck, and the very concrete experience of leading in French tech.
Recrutement, crises, décisions difficile: Hiring, crises, tough decisions, growth… or giving things up. Honest feedback, sometimes uncomfortable, often very enlightening — a real strategic watch on French Tech. With the necessary clear-eyed caveat: a CEO always tells the story with a bias… let's say, a positive one.
De temps en temps, un Français installé: Every so often, a French person based in the United States paints a broader picture — AI, economic cycles, crises, forecasts. Always without a crystal ball: "here's what I see, here's what I don't know".
Ton posé, ego absent. Sébastien ne cherc: Calm tone, no ego. Sébastien never tries to shine: he puts his guests forward, follows up when needed, reframes when necessary… then steps aside. Apple Podcasts rating: 4.9/5 — listeners know what's good.
Alex l'écoute « religieusement » et ne r: Alex listens "religiously" and never misses an episode — because it's a podcast that respects the listener's intelligence and time. The stable format isn't editorial laziness: it's a framework that showcases the substance, week after week, guest after guest.
C'est le podcast à écouter quand on veut: It's the podcast to listen to if you want to understand how French tech really works, through those who run it. Tech told by people with their hands in it — and for that alone, it's well worth a listen.
